dailyTopNewsBrief.headline: Ravens (4-7) Week 12 Briefing: Wednesday Injury Report Ahead of Texans
bullets: Injury & Practice Status: RB Derrick Henry (concussion), WR Rashod Bateman (groin), and WR Zay Flowers (ankle) logged limited practice reps Wednesday [Eric DeCosta](https://x.com/Ravens/status/2125728085148307816). DT Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring) and S Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) did not practice Wednesday, while CB Marlon Humphrey (personal) practiced in full [Eric DeCosta](https://x.com/Ravens/status/2125728085148307816).

Week 12 Texans Outlook: Jesse Minter and DC Anthony Weaver open installation for the Houston Texans (4-6, HOU -6.5, HC DeMeco Ryans, OC Nick Caley & DC Matt Burke (Road Test))—a unit ranked #3 in Field Goal % (95.2%) as Baltimore prepares for a pivotal AFC matchup [Jamison Hensley](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/50597502/henry-concussion-protocol-ravens-expect-play) [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/nfl/preview?gameId=401873085).

AFC Playoff Trajectory: Entering Week 12 at 4-7 (4th in AFC North • #11 Seed in AFC), Baltimore carries a 3.9% postseason projection, 0.1% AFC North division title mark, and 0% #1 Seed Bye equity into the conference stretch [NFL Trade Rumors](https://nfltraderumors.co/afc-notes-aaron-rodgers-mike-mccarthy-steelers-ravens/).

Around the Beat: Madubuike was unable to play against the Panthers in Week 11 due to a hamstring injury that he sustained against the Chargers in Week 10 [Jamison Hensley](https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/4035245/nnamdi-madubuike#:~:text=Madubuike%20%28hamstring%29%20did%20not%20participate%20in%20Wednesday's).

Before the Marlon Humphrey situation, the last time I can remember the Ravens deactivating a player as a disciplinary measure was 23 years ago, when Baltimore benched cornerback Chris McAlister.

In 2003, when the Ravens were practicing in San Diego because of a hurricane in Baltimore, McAlister missed curfew one…
rawStream.fullText:
Before the Marlon Humphrey situation, the last time I can remember the Ravens deactivating a player as a disciplinary measure was 23 years ago, when Baltimore benched cornerback Chris McAlister.

In 2003, when the Ravens were practicing in San Diego because of a hurricane in Baltimore, McAlister missed curfew one night and then skipped a morning team meeting. He reported back just as the team was prepared to leave the hotel for practice and was notified by coach Brian Billick that he would not accompany the team for the rest of the weekend.
